title: Introduce continuous phase batcher and realtime tail sampler
author: Aisha Menon
release_notes: Adds a new continuous-phase batching scheduler to the benchmark harness and a realtime tail sampler that exports p95/p99 token-latency traces; improves p99 stability for mixed-length workloads; no user-facing API changes.
description: Summary: Adds a continuous-phase batcher to the benchmark-lab harness and a lightweight realtime tail sampler that tags and exports extreme token-latency events for the reporting pipeline. Motivation: existing bursty-mix runners create large variance when short and long sequences are indiscriminately co-batched. The continuous-phase batcher groups requests by a phase metric (sequence-length percentile + warmup state) to produce batches with tighter intra-batch length distribution while allowing controlled backpressure ramping to avoid cold-start spikes. The tail sampler runs in-process during benchmark runs to capture per-token latency traces and emits compact protobuf records to the heartbeats reporter for downstream analysis (no persistent DB dependency). Implementation notes: - New scheduler module: bench/schedulers/continuous_phase.go. Implements a sliding-window histogram of recent seq lengths and computes a phase_id for each request. Batches are formed by phase-aware binning with a max-skew threshold and optional latency SLO guard. - Backpressure ramp: a per-pool gradient limiter that increases offered concurrency when observed p50 latency is below target, decreases when p95 exceeds threshold. This uses exponential smoothing and a cooldown timer to avoid oscillation. - Realtime tail sampler: bench/samplers/realtime_tail_sampler.go; samples hard-tail events (token latency > dynamic threshold) and attaches context (model, seq_len, kernel_hint) before publishing to reporter via an existing /reporter/collector API. Records are size-limited and include a short stack of scheduler decisions. - Test harness: new unit tests and an e2e scenario in bench/testdata/mix-phase-run.yaml that reproduces a bimodal sequence mix and asserts reduced p99 variance. - Reporter wiring: updates reporter/ingest to accept compact tail records and a new reporter/transform/tail-annotator that enriches traces with kernel and batch composition metadata. - Opt-in flag: continuous phase batching is feature-gated behind BENCH_PHASE_BATCHER=true to avoid affecting other repos until rollout. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-5241) - [x] Unit tests for scheduler and sampler - [x] E2E regression scenario added - [x] Backpressure safety limits / cooldown implemented - [x] Telemetry formats documented in reporter README - [x] Feature flag added for controlled rollout Commits: - 5c3b8f2: initial continuous phase batcher implementation and scheduler tests - a23d7b1: realtime tail sampler and exporter wiring - 4f9e118: e2e mix-phase-run scenario and baseline traces - 90b2e0d: reporter ingest + transform plumbing and lightweight schema - d12a77c: feature flag, docs, and minor flake fixes Changed files (high level): - bench/schedulers/continuous_phase.go - bench/samplers/realtime_tail_sampler.go - bench/schedulers/continuous_phase_test.go - bench/testdata/mix-phase-run.yaml - reporter/collector/ingest.go (small change: added TailRecord path) - reporter/transform/tail_annotator.go - docs/bench/phase-batcher.md - ci/bench-e2e.yaml (added new scenario) - BUILD.bazel (new deps) Small illustrative diffs: - continuous_phase.go: core batching loop (simplified) "for req := range q { phase := phaseHistogram.Bucket(req.SeqLen); scheduler.AssignToBin(phase, req) }" - realtime_tail_sampler.go: emission logic "if tokenLatency > sampler.DynamicThreshold() { collector.Publish(TailRecord{...}) }" Review conversation (condensed into single-threaded summary): - Samir Rao (reviewer) 2026-02-20: "Nice approach — two questions: 1) do we risk starving very short sequences when binning with long ones? 2) can the sampler add measurable CPU overhead under extreme load?" - Aisha (author) 2026-02-21: "Addressed both: bins have a short-request priority quota and the backpressure ramp avoids unbounded queue growth; sampler uses a cheap moving-threshold and samples at most 1/1000 tokens by default, CPU overhead measured <1% in local run — numbers added to design doc." - Elena Garcia (reviewer) 2026-02-24: "Please add clearer schema versioning for tail records so we can evolve the annotator without breaking downstream parsers." - Aisha 2026-02-25: "Added schema_version field and a tiny compatibility shim in reporter/collector; updated docs." - Tom Briggs (approver) 2026-03-01: "Perf numbers look good in staging; LGTM." CI summary: - bazel/test:bench-unit — pass - bench/e2e (ci/bench-e2e.yaml) — pass (staging run measured p99 variance down ~22% versus baseline) - lint/gofmt — pass - security/snyk — pass - perf/regression-check — pass (no regression) There was one transient failure on bench/e2e on the first run due to a flaky timing assertion; rerun passed. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-03-03 by Tom Briggs, commit message summarizes the feature and links ENG-5241. Notes on rollout and follow-ups: - Feature will be enabled behind BENCH_PHASE_BATCHER in canary runs for 2 weeks before wider staging. - Follow-up work: add an adaptive phase-compression heuristic (ENG-5350) and integrate with the kernel selection telemetry so the annotator can surface which kernels are implicated in tail events. - Ops: reporter retention for tail records is limited to 7d by default; a pipeline job will downsample and keep pinned exemplars for 90d for long-term analysis. Compatibility/impact: no changes to public APIs; opt-in flag prevents accidental changes to other teams. If issues surface, revert via toggling BENCH_PHASE_BATCHER=false or reverting the single squash commit. Related PRs/Tickets: ENG-5241 (design doc), ENG-5350 (follow-up heuristics), PERF-INC-77 (incident note: flagged earlier cold-start spikes), RFC-bench-phase (design discussion).
